title: Senior Software Engineer, Backend - New Verticals
description:
Our Global Structure 

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Senior Software Engineer

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day.

From real-time logistics to resilient infrastructure and marketplace optimisation, we design, build and operate technology that powers Deliveroo’s growth at scale.

In November 2023 we launched our non-food retail offering, Deliveroo ‘Shopping’, where we work with large and small merchants. We oversee all operations within the grocery and retail ecosystem, ensuring stores are equipped to receive and efficiently process orders. Our solutions empower stores to manage orders seamlessly through multiple channels, including our in-house app, API integration, and devices pre-installed with our software. Additionally, we provide tools to maintain and update product catalogs, ensuring accurate inventory for consumers. The technology we’ve developed enables our partners to pick the correct items swiftly while keeping inventory data current, optimizing both efficiency and accuracy.

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our London (Hybrid - 3 days from the office) team. In this role, you’ll help us improve code structure and architecture while leading team project planning to maximise efficiency and reliability across our production systems.

Get to know our Engineering team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

What You’ll Be Doing 

Here’s what your day-to-day might look like:

- 
Drive Technical Excellence: Improve code structure and architecture across your team’s remit, developing, releasing and running large-scale web applications whilst transitioning our monolithic codebase to a microservice-based architecture

- 
Lead Project Planning: Foresee dependencies and risks, partnering closely with Product and Design to ensure smooth delivery of complex features, whilst defining the backend architecture and tech stack for a product area

- 
Optimise Operations: Improve performance, reliability, scalability and security for our backend systems

- 
Collaborate & Influence: Build relationships across global engineering teams to identify collaboration opportunities and influence the wider technical roadmap.

- 
Mentor & Hire: Support the personal growth of your colleagues through technical guidance and take an active role in conducting engineering interviews to scale our team.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

- Proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software 

- Strong Engineering Principles: Deep pride in writing readable, well-designed, and well-tested software.

- Backend Expertise: Significant experience building web-based applications (we use Go, Ruby/Rails, Python, Scala, and Rust).

- Data Proficiency: Practical experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL) and "NoSQL" backends like Redis, DynamoDB, or ElasticSearch.

- Systems at Scale: Proven ability to manage web architecture at scale (handling 20krpm and above).

- Technical Leadership: Experience breaking down large pieces of work and guiding implementation choices for a team of engineers.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving. We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community organisers, proud parents, and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.

🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you’re rewarded for the impact you make.

➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog .

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Explore our Engineering Interview Guide here to help you feel confident at each stage.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!

Privacy 

Deliveroo will process your personal information in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy .

Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness .

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data Platform
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA or Remote (U.S.)

Location : This role is remote in the United States, Canada, or some countries in South America.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. 

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients. 

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you. 

How you’ll make an impact 

You will join the Data Services team - one of three teams in a data platform group of about ten engineers, alongside infrastructure and developer productivity.

- Work closely with data analysts, data engineers, and machine learning engineers to understand their needs - and evolve the Doximity data stack to meet them.

- Build the foundations that make client-facing data delivery safe and repeatable - per-client data isolation, access controls, and auditability.

- Build and operate the MCP-based tooling and agentic workflows through which analysts and clients interact with the data platform - and the data it manifests - by conversation rather than tickets.

- Work in a HIPAA-regulated environment where the right people and systems reach the data they need and nothing more - masking policies, scoped roles, audit trails, and approval gates that hold up to scrutiny from auditors and clients alike.

- Understand what our data product teams are trying to achieve, and design solutions that maximize the time they spend on their goals and minimize the time lost to technical hurdles.

- Help strengthen our software engineering culture within the data organization, leading by example.

- Diagnose development, performance, and stability issues in our core data pipelines and Python libraries, and help product data teams resolve problems that need platform-level expertise.

What we’re looking for 

- We’re seeking a strong Python engineer who brings deep professional experience in data engineering and internal tooling, with a track record of supporting multiple product teams simultaneously.

- Especially valuable experience:

- Snowflake beyond querying - governance features, cloning, Time Travel and Fail-safe, hybrid tables, streams, and data lifecycle capabilities, Cortex suite of AI tools, Snowpark Container Services, or data sharing.

- Kafka, change data capture (CDC) like Debezium, and database internals - a significant portion of our pipeline work lives here.

- Operating under HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar - least-privilege design, masking and de-identification, audit logging.

- Building or operating agentic and MCP-based tooling.

- Apache Airflow and AWS.

- Container-based development workflows (Kubernetes, Docker) - useful, but secondary to the above.

- We don’t expect all of these. Depth in Python, SQL, and data engineering is the requirement; the rest tells us where you’ll ramp fastest.

- The ideal candidate will demonstrate expert fluency in Python and an understanding of programming language internals.

- Advanced knowledge of software engineering practices and testing methodologies is a must; you are foremost an engineer, making you passionate about high-quality code, automated testing, and software engineering best practices. You demonstrate this both within your own team and with colleagues beyond it.

- You have deep fluency in SQL, using analytical databases, and are able to practically employ and orchestrate user defined functions, stored procedures, and other database-oriented solutions to deliver performant and cost-effective database-driven solutions.

- You have worked with data that carries real handling obligations - PHI, PII, or client-confidential data - under a framework like HIPAA, SOC 2, or GDPR. You design for least-privilege access by default, you think in terms of blast radius and auditability, and you treat these as engineering problems rather than paperwork.

- Your ability and drive to self-manage, prioritize tasks, and deliver functional solutions will be crucial to succeeding in this role.

- You treat AI-driven engineering as part of the craft, not a novelty - agentic coding tools, MCP-based tooling, and automation that removes toil - and you invest in keeping your practice current as the tools evolve. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, and you keep your work legible through practices like clear change management and well-documented code. You see your teammates as your first customer.

About Us 

- Explore our stack 

- We have over 500 private repositories in Github containing our pipelines, our own internal multi-functional tools, and open-source projects 

- We have worked as a distributed team for a long time; we're currently about 65% distributed 

- Find out more information on the Doximity engineering blog 

- Our company core values 

- Our recruiting process 

- Our product development cycle 

- Our on-boarding & mentorship process 

Compensation 

The anticipated total compensation for this role is $165,000 - $227,000, depending on factors such as experience, skills, location, and internal equity.

Our total compensation package may include:

- Base salary

- Equity (where applicable)

Specific compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.

Benefits 

In addition to competitive compensation, Doximity offers a comprehensive benefits package for full time employees. Some of our offerings include:

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance

- 401(k) with company match

- Flexible paid time off and company holidays

- Paid parental leave

- Professional development and learning opportunities

- Wellness and mental health resources

- Remote work support and home office stipend (where applicable)

Why You'll Love Working Here 

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

- Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

- Work with exceptional teammates. Collaborate with thoughtful, talented colleagues who value curiosity, humility, and continuous learning.

- Enjoy flexibility and trust. We support flexible ways of working and empower employees with the autonomy to own their work.

- Grow your career. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, and shape your career through mentorship and professional development.

- Bring your authentic self. We're committed to fostering an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives are welcomed, respected, and celebrated.

Our Hiring Process & AI Tools 

Doximity may use artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools throughout the hiring process to help improve the candidate experience and support our recruiting team. These tools may assist with administrative tasks such as scheduling, general communication, interview coordination, note-taking, or summarizing interview feedback. Human recruiters and hiring managers make all hiring decisions. We are committed to using AI responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable laws.

Equal Employment Opportunity 

Doximity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Account
description:
Lemonway is a licensed payment institution at the heart of Europe’s new digital economy. 

We secure payments for crowdfunding platforms, the collaborative economy, marketplaces and online retailers, with a strong commitment to fighting fraud and protecting funds. 

Regulated by the ACPR and benefiting from the European passport in 29 countries, Lemonway is based in Paris and Hamburg and brings together 150 multicultural and committed Lemonheroes . 

More than 400 marketplaces trust us. We manage 1.4 million user wallets and have raised €50 million from Breega, Speedinvest and Toscafund. 

Profitable for the past four years and growing by 25% in 2025, Lemonway aims to remain one of Europe’s leading payment providers through healthy and sustainable growth. 

About the Team 

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer for the Account Tribe , who build a critical part of our platform powering the compliance experience across channels. You will be led by John, the Engineering Manager of the Tribe, and work closely with 6 engineers across 2 squads : Comply, and Manage.

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. 

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. 

Where this is going 

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. 

Why this role exists 

Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening. 

How we work 

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own 

Everything on the screen:

- The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.

- The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.

- The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.

- Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.

- The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins. 

We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for 

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team 

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

You’ll join our five-person Architecture team and work closely with the AI PMO, connecting business teams with architecture, product, engineering, data and security.

Seniority here means tackling more complex challenges, having greater autonomy and impact, and helping others grow. We’re looking for someone who has recent practical experience building technical solutions and wants to continue doing so. You’ll design, prototype, configure, integrate and build, while also providing technical direction when needed.

Location: Rotterdam (Hybrid – 50% in office)

Your impact 

- Lead complex AI discovery 
Turn unclear, cross-functional or strategically important business challenges into concrete AI opportunities. Take them from problem definition and validation through to a working prototype.

Design, develop, configure and test agents, assistants and automated workflows that connect different departments, data sources and systems. You won’t only define what should be built or hand it over to others. You’ll be actively involved in building it.

Identify when an AI solution needs to move beyond experimentation into a business-critical or customer-facing product, and work with product and engineering teams to make that transition successful.

Develop approaches for grounding, identity, integration, monitoring and evaluation that can be reused across teams, and identify opportunities for shared AI capabilities.

Review solutions, share technical expertise and coach colleagues and business users. You’ll work closely with our AI Solution Specialist and help raise the quality of AI solutions across Sunweb Group, while remaining an active builder yourself.

You’re curious, pragmatic and comfortable navigating ambiguity. You combine strong technical judgement with the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

You know the difference between an impressive AI demo and a solution that creates measurable business value. You enjoy working independently, bringing different perspectives together and sharing what you learn along the way.

Most importantly, you’re a builder. You enjoy getting hands-on with technology, experimenting, developing prototypes and turning ideas into working solutions. - Experience taking ambiguous business problems from discovery through prototyping, testing and solution design

- Experience working with AI agents, assistants or orchestration workflows

Our AI and technology landscape includes Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, Power Automate, Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft Graph, Azure AI services, Microsoft Foundry, ChatGPT/OpenAI, Claude/Anthropic, MCP, Entra ID and Git.

Sunweb Group is one of Europe’s largest online travel agencies, sending over 1.3 million holidaymakers annually to unforgettable destinations. title: Cloud Systems Administrator
description:
Headquarters: 

URL: https://oneimaging.com 

Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.

The Systems Administrator owns the day-to-day administration of our SaaS and cloud vendor stack, with security and logging as the first priority. You will manage user access across every platform we use, keep audit logging and security controls configured and reviewed, write scripts to automate repetitive admin work, and act as a first responder on security incidents. You will also provide hands-on IT support to employees. This is a generalist role for someone who likes owning systems end to end: you are the person who knows how each vendor is set up, who has access to what, and where the logs live. 

What you'll do: 

Vendor and SaaS administration (security and logging first) 

- Serve as the primary administrator for our SaaS and cloud platforms: tenant settings, SSO/SAML and SCIM integration, MFA enforcement, API keys, roles and permissions.

- Configure and maintain audit logging on every platform that supports it; centralize logs where possible and make sure retention meets our compliance needs.

- Run periodic access reviews, remove stale accounts and over-privileged roles, and keep an accurate inventory of who has admin rights where.

- Own the security posture of each vendor: review security settings on new tools before rollout, track vendor security notices, and evaluate new vendor requests for risk.

User lifecycle and identity

- Onboard and offboard employees and contractors across all systems the same day, driven from Rippling and Google Workspace, our identity sources of truth.

- Manage groups, roles and licenses; keep license counts right-sized and flag waste.

- Maintain device enrollment, MDM policies and endpoint security for company laptops.

Scripting and automation

- Write and maintain scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) and use vendor APIs to automate provisioning, access reviews, log collection and reporting.

- Build lightweight integrations between systems (for example, HRIS to identity provider to SaaS) so manual admin work shrinks over time.

Security incident response

- Act as a first responder on security alerts: triage, contain (disable accounts, revoke tokens, isolate devices), gather evidence from logs, and escalate.

- Participate in post-incident reviews and implement the fixes that come out of them.

- Help maintain and test our incident response and business continuity runbooks.

IT support

- Provide tier 1–2 support to employees: hardware, accounts, access, video conferencing, printers and office network.

- Procure, image and manage laptops and peripherals; keep an asset inventory current.

- Write and keep up internal how-to documentation so common requests become self-service.

Platforms you will administer

These are our largest software and cloud vendors by spend over the last 12 months. Deep experience with the first group is expected; the rest you will pick up on the job.

Area

Platforms

Cloud infrastructure

Amazon Web Services (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub)

Identity, HR and devices

Rippling (HRIS, SSO, device management) and Google Workspace, used together as our identity source of truth

Productivity and email

Google Workspace (admin console, Vault, security center)

Customer support and CRM

Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom

Communications

Zoom, Aircall, Twilio

Data and engineering

Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, Sentry, Linear, Postman, Stytch

AI platforms

Anthropic, OpenAI (API key and usage management)

Collaboration and design

Notion, Lucid, Figma, Adobe, Scribe

Security tools

NordVPN Teams, Virtru (email encryption)

Healthcare operations

Waystar, AdvancedMD

Marketing and recruiting

Braze, ActiveCampaign, Greenhouse, LinkedIn

About you: 

- 3+ years administering SaaS and cloud platforms in a company of 50–500 people, including Google Workspace and an identity/HR platform like Rippling or Okta, and ideally AWS.

- Hands-on experience configuring SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, MFA policies and role-based access.

- Working knowledge of audit logging and log review: you know what a CloudTrail event, a Workspace audit log or a Zendesk audit entry looks like and what to do with it.

- Scripting ability in at least one of Python, PowerShell or Bash, and comfort calling REST APIs.

- Experience responding to security incidents (phishing, compromised accounts, lost devices) and documenting what happened.

- Strong IT support instincts: you communicate clearly with non-technical colleagues and close tickets fast.

- Familiarity with HIPAA or a comparable compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and what it means for access control and logging.

Nice to have:

- AWS Certified SysOps Administrator, Security Specialty, or Google Workspace Administrator certification.

- Experience with a SIEM or log aggregation tool (Datadog, Splunk, Google SecOps, or similar) and writing detection rules.

- MDM experience (Rippling, Jamf, Kandji, Intune) and macOS/Windows endpoint hardening.

- Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code for managing AWS and SaaS configuration.

- Prior work in a healthcare or other regulated company.

- Experience administering API usage and keys for AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI) and setting spend and access controls.

The base salary range for this position is $60,000 - $75,000. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans.

🌍 About Zauber 

After co-founding and scaling Forto to over $600M in funding, I took a step back to reflect on what’s still broken in global logistics. The answer was clear: it’s still a human-first, spreadsheet-heavy industry, full of repetitive processes and broken system interoperability.

With the rise of AI agents, we now have the tools to rethink that from the ground up. Zauber builds autonomous agents for the global logistics industry, AI workers that handle operational tasks, talk to systems and humans alike, and get better every day.

🚢 We're already live with global logistics leaders in Europe and Asia 

💰 Backed by P9 - one of Europe's top early-stage funds 

📈 Growing fast and hiring exceptional engineers to join early 

Now we are looking for an exceptional Product Engineer to help us define and build the next generation of AI-powered logistics systems.

🧠 What You'll Do 

You will help turn vision into product and bring our first AI agents into the hands of real users. This is a high-ownership role, working closely with the founding team and customers to build something truly new. You'll operate across the full stack—talking to customers one hour and debugging an agent loop the next—making the foundational technical decisions that define what the product becomes.

• Talk directly to customers and translate their needs into product direction and system architecture

• Build full-stack features that combine intuitive interfaces with intelligent backend logic, including LLM orchestration, agent workflows, and structured data pipelines

• Push the limits of what LLMs and agents can do in production, working through the hard problems of reliability, latency, and evaluation

• Scale from demo-quality code to robust, production-ready systems, making deliberate tradeoffs between speed and durability as the product matures

• Help shape the technical vision and product strategy of the company

👤 You Might Be a Fit If You... 

• Have experience taking full ownership of technical projects, from architecture through to delivery and iteration

• Are pragmatic and fast in the early days, but know when to raise the bar for scale and quality

• Love writing and shipping code, and are not afraid to throw it away when the problem shifts

• Enjoy speaking with users and iterating quickly based on feedback, treating customer insight as a core input to engineering decisions

• Want to build something ambitious and impactful, from the very beginning

🛠 What You Bring 

• Strong skills in Node.js, TypeScript, and React, with an instinct for patterns that move fast without creating debt—clean service boundaries, event-driven architectures, thin abstractions that are easy to replace

• Experience with distributed systems and serverless infrastructure that handle concurrency, failure, and scale

• Hands-on MongoDB experience, including schema design that balances query performance with flexibility

• Familiarity with observability tooling, ideally Datadog—tracing across async workflows, using metrics to debug production issues, not just monitor them

• Experience with modern AI tooling: LLMs, vector stores, embedding pipelines, prompt engineering

title: Senior Software Engineer, Query
description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote), United States (Remote), United Kingdom (Remote) Mexico City, Mexico - Hybrid

About CircleCI Engineering

CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.

At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About the Query Team

Every pipeline, job, and test that runs on CircleCI generates data, and that history is one of our biggest advantages in an agentic software delivery lifecycle. Flaky test detection, test insights, pipeline search, and agents that reason about why a build failed all depend on fast, reliable access to it.

The Query team owns the system that makes this possible. We pull product data out of the transactional services that create it and store it in datastores built for historical and analytical workloads. We serve it through domain-level APIs to CircleCI's product teams and to customers through our public API. Our goal is to make storing data "fire and forget" for every other team, and querying it fast and dependable at a scale that keeps growing.

What You'll Do

- Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.

- Shape how we store data at scale. Own and harden our ClickHouse-based storage layer. Design schemas for known and emerging access patterns, and tune ingestion and query performance to support production-scale data.

- Build the pipelines that move our data. Design and own ingestion from event streams and durable workflows built on Temporal. Data should arrive reliably, stay queryable while it's in transit, and never slow down the critical path of the services that produce it.

- Serve data to the product and to customers. Evolve our platform into the default path for historical queries. Make getting historical data easy, not a bottleneck. Teams should be able to get what they need quickly and with minimal hand-holding, while Query keeps enough visibility into how the data is used to optimize ingestion and reads across every consumer. Build in the indexing, caching, and tiered storage required to keep it performant.

- Set technical direction. When the problem is complex or the answer isn't obvious, you lead the design discussion, write up the architecture decision, and make the call. You help decide which data domain we migrate next and how.

- Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand ingestion lag, query latency, and data correctness. For a data platform, operational data drives stability, not just incident response.

- Keep things moving. You take ambiguous data problems from design to production quickly, and you help the people around you move faster too.

You don't just patch problems, you ask why they happened. You'll fix the immediate issue, then solve the underlying team practice, process, or system that let it through.

What You'll Bring

- AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.

- Hands-on data experience. You've built or owned data-intensive systems such as ingestion pipelines, event-driven architectures, or analytical and time-series datastores. You understand the tradeoffs between transactional and analytical storage, and you've designed schemas and tuned queries for high-volume workloads. Experience with ClickHouse or another columnar database is a strong plus.

- Backend depth in Go. You're strong in Go, or strong in a comparable language and eager to work in Go: interface design, data modeling, service integration, and concurrency. Familiarity with React and TypeScript is a plus, since you'll occasionally work on the product surfaces that display this data.

- Distributed systems judgment. You understand delivery guarantees, idempotency, backpressure, and failure recovery. You know when to rely on a framework's reliability guarantees rather than building your own.

- Technical leadership. You've led the design of complex systems and made tradeoffs deliberately. You leave foundations others can build on. You raise the quality bar through reviews, mentoring, and direct feedback, not just through the code you write.

- A track record of shipping. 5+ years building and operating production backend systems. Your work has served real users, and you've treated latency, reliability, and correctness as design concerns.

Sound like you?

You care about how data powers the product, not just where it lives. You know how to make a datastore fast at scale, and have tuned schemas and queries against real production load. You think like a platform engineer, measuring your work by how much it unblocks the teams building on it. AI isn't a tool you reach for occasionally; it's a core part of how you approach and solve problems. If that sounds like you, we want to talk.

About CircleCI 

CircleCI is the world’s largest continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform, and the hub where code moves from idea to delivery. As one of the most-used DevOps tools - processing more than 3 million jobs a day - CircleCI has unique access to data on how the most effective engineering teams work, and the tools to help software companies successfully leverage the power of AI into their commercial applications. Companies like Hinge, HuggingFace, and Samsung use us to improve engineering team productivity, release better products, and get to market faster.

How CircleCI Uses AI in Hiring 

At CircleCI, people make our hiring decisions. We use technology to support our recruiting team so they can spend more time on what matters most: getting to know you.

Where we may use AI

We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Data 

At Gemini, our Data Team is the engine that powers insight, innovation, and trust across the company. We bring together world-class data engineers, platform engineers, machine learning engineers, analytics engineers, and data scientists — all working in harmony to transform raw information into secure, reliable, and actionable intelligence. From building scalable pipelines and platforms, to enabling cutting-edge machine learning, to ensuring governance and cost efficiency, we deliver the foundation for smarter decisions and breakthrough products. We thrive at the intersection of crypto, technology, and finance, and we’re united by a shared mission: to unlock the full potential of Gemini’s data to drive growth, efficiency, and customer impact.

The Role: Senior Data Engineer 

The Data team is responsible for designing and operating the data infrastructure that powers insight, reporting, analytics, and machine learning across the business. As a Senior Data Engineer, you will contribute to architectural decisions, mentor junior engineers, and build high-scale systems that have meaningful impact on your team and the teams you partner with. You will own the end-to-end delivery of data products within your domain, and partner closely with product, analytics, ML, finance, operations, and engineering teams to move, transform, and model data reliably, with observability, resilience, and agility.

Responsibilities: 

- Design, build, and maintain data infrastructure and pipelines spanning both batch and real-time / streaming workloads, contributing to architectural decisions along the way

- Build and maintain scalable, efficient, and reliable ETL/ELT pipelines using languages and frameworks such as Python, SQL, Spark, Flink, Beam, or equivalents

- Work on real-time or near-real-time data solutions (e.g. CDC, streaming, micro-batch) for use cases that require timely data

- Partner with data scientists, ML engineers, analysts, and product teams to understand data requirements, define SLAs, and deliver coherent data products that others can self-serve

- Establish data quality, validation, observability, and monitoring frameworks (data auditing, alerting, anomaly detection, data lineage)

- Investigate and resolve complex production issues: root cause analysis, performance bottlenecks, data integrity, fault tolerance

- Document data flows, data dictionaries, architecture patterns, and operational runbooks

Minimum Qualifications: 

- 5+ years of experience in data engineering (or similar) roles

- Strong experience in ETL/ELT pipeline design, implementation, and optimization

- Deep expertise in Python and SQL writing production-quality, maintainable, testable code

- Experience with large-scale data warehouses (e.g. Databricks, BigQuery, Snowflake)

- Solid grounding in software engineering fundamentals, data structures, and systems thinking

- Hands-on experience in data modeling (dimensional modeling, normalization, schema design)

- Experience building systems with real-time or streaming data (e.g. Kafka, Kinesis, Flink, Spark Streaming), and familiarity with CDC frameworks

- Experience with orchestration / workflow frameworks (e.g. Airflow)

- Familiarity with data governance, lineage, metadata, cataloging, and data quality practices

Preferred Qualifications: 

- Experience with crypto, financial services, trading, markets, or exchange systems

- Experience with blockchain, crypto, Web3 data — e.g. blocks, transactions, contract calls, token transfers, UTXO/account models, on-chain indexing, chain APIs, etc.

- Experience with infrastructure as code, containerization, and CI/CD pipelines

- Hands-on experience managing and optimizing Databricks on AWS

It Pays to Work Here 

The compensation & benefits package for this role includes:

- Competitive starting pay

- A discretionary annual bonus

- Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant

- Comprehensive health plans

- 401K with company matching

- Paid Parental Leave

- Flexible time off

Salary Range : The base salary range for this role is between $126,000 - $180,000 in the State of New York. This range is not inclusive of our discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Expectations may vary by location and role, so candidates are encouraged to connect with their recruiter to learn more about the specific policy for the role. Employees who do not live near one of our hubs are part of our remote workforce. All employees, however, are required to onboard in-person at one of our office locations.

title: Paid Media Specialist
description:
Kinsta is one of the top providers of managed hosting for WordPress, with a growing club of 230,000+ businesses including startups, universities, and Fortune 500 firms. We're motivated by excellent quality and proud to have received a 97% satisfaction rating from our customers.

That's because, to us, each day is a chance to grow. As a team, we continuously inspire each other to learn new and better ways to make an impact. We own our jobs proudly - our leaders don't hold our hands, but they're in our corner whenever we ask for help - and our environment is flexible and remote-first.

As our new Paid Media Specialist, you'll plan, run, and optimize paid social advertising campaigns for Kinsta. You'll join our Performance Marketing team, report to the Paid Media Team Lead, and work closely with Demand Generation, Design, and RevOps to deliver a consistent volume of sign-ups and revenue that supports Kinsta's growth goals. It's a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable with data and enjoys testing new ideas.

Your focus is Kinsta's paid social presence across LinkedIn, Meta, Reddit, X, and other relevant platforms. You'll reach the businesses, agencies, and enterprises that run their sites on WordPress, through campaigns that cover the full funnel from awareness to customer acquisition.

You'll own campaigns from build to optimization, keep conversion tracking reliable, and turn performance data into clear recommendations. We work with teams across the globe, so you should be used to collaborating asynchronously and flexible enough to join the occasional early or late call. The ideal Kinsta Paid Media Specialist is analytical, detail-oriented, curious, proactive, and collaborative.

What You Will Do:

Plan, build, launch, and manage paid social campaigns across LinkedIn, Meta, Reddit, X, and other relevant platforms, covering the full funnel from awareness and demand generation to lead generation and customer acquisition.

Monitor performance and continuously optimize targeting, bidding strategies, budgets, ad creatives, and landing pages, scaling what works while keeping acquisition costs efficient.

Run audience research and competitive analysis to find new opportunities for growth.

Develop and run A/B tests across ad messaging, creative assets, audiences, and landing pages.

Own conversion tracking: implement, maintain, and troubleshoot it through Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), and platform-specific pixels and tags, and work with marketing and technical teams to keep conversion events and attribution accurate.

Analyze campaign performance using ad platform data, web analytics, and CRM reporting, and build reports and dashboards that share results and actionable insights.

Collaborate with content, design, product marketing, and sales on ad copy, creative concepts, and campaign assets that match our messaging and business priorities.

Support our paid media strategy: follow advertising trends and platform updates, and recommend ways to improve campaign efficiency, lead quality, and overall marketing ROI.

Use AI tools to streamline research, reporting, ad copy, and creative ideation, automate repetitive tasks, and apply critical thinking to AI-generated recommendations so decisions stay grounded in accurate data and business objectives.

What You Bring To The Role:

2-4 years of hands-on experience independently building, launching, managing, and optimizing paid social campaigns, including on Meta, LinkedIn, and Reddit, ideally in hosting, B2B technology, or a related industry.

Practical experience setting up and troubleshooting conversion tracking with Google Tag Manager, GA4, and advertising platform pixels or conversion tags.

A strong understanding of core paid media metrics, including CPC, CPM, CTR, conversion rate, CPA, and ROAS, and experience analyzing campaign data and turning findings into actionable optimizations.

Familiarity with audience targeting, retargeting, and campaign testing methodologies, and an understanding of marketing funnels, attribution, and how paid media contributes to lead generation and customer acquisition.

Attention to detail, a proactive approach to problem-solving, and excellent organizational and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns and priorities at once.

Bonus if you have:

Experience running paid media campaigns for B2B SaaS, hosting, PaaS, or other technical products, and familiarity with WordPress or cloud platforms.

Experience with CRM, marketing automation, and attribution or reporting tools such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Looker Studio, Dreamdata, or HockeyStack.

Knowledge of advanced conversion tracking, including enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports, and server-side tracking, plus a basic understanding of HTML, JavaScript, cookies, and how tracking tags work on websites.

Experience optimizing landing pages and collaborating on conversion rate optimization (CRO) initiatives.

Proficiency in other languages and experience managing non-English paid media campaigns

Experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT or Claude to improve campaign workflows, analysis, and creative development.

Annual remote expense budget.

Flexible PTO.

Paid parental leave.

Annual professional development budget: available after one year with Kinsta.

Sabbatical: available after three years with Kinsta (and every three years thereafter).

Location-specific healthcare benefits (includes vision and dental) for employees hired in the USA, UK, Canada, and Hungary.

Pension plan for employees hired in the UK, and 401k contributions for employees hired in the USA.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries. 

The team 

To sustain the company's growth, Ledger is looking for a Senior Scala Backend Engineer to join the Cloud Wallet team . This team builds and operates the backend services that power blockchain account management, transaction processing and on-chain data aggregation across all Ledger wallet surfaces, from Ledger Live to Ledger Enterprise, the custody platform used by financial institutions. Every client transaction goes through these services, and so does every new blockchain Ledger supports. We believe in the power of functional programming to build robust and scalable platforms. We take time to share, challenge, and grow together through bi-weekly knowledge-sharing sessions, meetups, conferences, and open source contributions.

What you’ll be doing 

- Design, build and operate the Scala services that connect Ledger wallets and the Ledger Enterprise platform to blockchain backends: account creation, operation history, transaction crafting, broadcast and lifecycle tracking.

- Lead new blockchain integrations end to end, from the integration design (ADR) to production, across account-based, UTXO and privacy-preserving chains.

- Own production quality on your scope: SLIs and SLOs, observability, distributed tracing. Take part in the firefighting rotation and drive incidents to resolution, including those raised by institutional clients.

- Define clear contracts with the Coin Integration and Ledger Enterprise teams, for example where UTXO selection lives or how transaction states are exposed to consumers.

- Write and review ADRs, challenge designs, and raise the bar on code quality, testing (including end-to-end on testnets) and technical debt management.

- Work in an AI-native way: use coding agents daily, write the specifications, constraints and verification that let them deliver safely, and contribute to the team's AI tooling.

- Mentor other engineers and share your knowledge across the Backend Blockchain community.

You will collaborate cross-functionally with: 

- The Coin Integration team for coin modules and new blockchain integrations.

- The Ledger Enterprise team, main consumer of the team's services for institutional custody.

- The Ledger Wallet, Ledger Button and Wallet XP teams as consumers of the team's backend APIs.

- The Blockchain platform team for data model alignment, indexing and event streaming.

- The Infrastructure and SRE teams for deployment, reliability and scalability.

- The Security team (Donjon) for vulnerability analysis and remediation.

- The Product team for roadmap prioritization and customer-driven requirements.

What we’re looking for 

- 5+ years of backend engineering, with real production ownership of distributed systems.

- Strong production experience

- Interest for Scala and functional programming practice

- Hands-on blockchain integration experience: transaction lifecycle, fees, finality, reorgs, on at least two models among account-based, UTXO and privacy-preserving chains.

- Experience with event-driven systems and data infrastructure (PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, NATS or equivalent) and with observability tooling (Datadog or equivalent).

- Able to diagnose an incident across several services and own the outcome, from root cause to fix in production.

- Comfortable reading and contributing to TypeScript code, as the team works on a polyglot stack.

- Daily use of AI coding tools, with a critical eye on their output.

- Clear written communication in English, especially for design documents and incident reports.

At Ledger, we are dedicated to continually investing in our employees which is why we offer more than just salaries; we provide comprehensive compensation packages that include a wide range of benefits. Here are some of the benefits you can look forward to:

- Flexible work options - Our hybrid policy allows employees to work from home up to 3 times per week

- Health & Wellness support - Health and Life Insurance.

- Financial growth opportunities - Employees can become shareholders in Ledger as well as other financial benefits depending on your country of work.

- Commuter allowance - Ledger offers a commuter allowance to contribute to your preferred means of transportation.

- Learning & Development - A comprehensive suite of training solutions providing a personalised learning experience for every employee.

For regionally specific benefits, your Talent Acquisition contact will be able to provide you with more information.

We’re committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need any adjustments or accommodations, just let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Vehicle Configuration Platform
description:
About Us 

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary 

A single firmware release must serve every vehicle variant we build across both Rivian and all Volkswagen brands. The vehicle configuration platform that the OTA team supports makes that possible: a schema-driven system that defines every configurable attribute of a vehicle and provisions them onto vehicles in the factory, in service, and over the air customer updates. Getting this wrong can mean anything from the wrong information showing on the driver display to a car that needs to be towed in for service.

You will be a technical leader on the team that owns this platform, working as a peer to its lead architect. Where the architect drives the structural evolution of the configuration system itself, you will own the health, reliability, and scalability of everything around it: the compilation and code generation pipelines, the validation and release infrastructure, the provisioning path from schema to vehicle, and the developer experience of every engineer who touches configuration. Over the past two years the technical security workload has grown on every front: a larger and more regulated customer base sending their own scans and security assessments, a wider detection and response scope, more infrastructure to keep hardened and auditable, and a growing backlog of security engineering projects that never reach the top of the queue. 

We are creating this position to add real technical capacity on the infrastructure side of security, and to move part of our security posture from manual effort to automated guardrails. You will be the bridge between security and platform engineering: deep enough in infrastructure to fix things yourself, and close enough to security operations to know what to look for.

That means direct impact and no layers between you and the decision. Roughly half of this role is greenfield build work you will own end to end.” Guillaume Seigneuret, CISO and Hiring Coach. 

Within 1 month, you will:

Complete our onboarding and learn how we work through our own platform and our Convexity culture

Map our Azure and AKS environment, our detection and logging coverage, and our ISO 27001 and SOC 2 control scope with the CISO and the Security Engineer

Meet the DevOps, platform engineering and IT teams you will work with daily

Within 3 months, you will: 

- 
Be autonomous on our AKS and Azure environment and handle infrastructure related alerts end to end 

- 
Have shipped at least one concrete hardening or automation improvement in production

Own the infrastructure scope of vulnerability management, from triage to remediation follow up

- 
Have measurably widened SIEM connector coverage, with documented log sources and retention 

- 
Run infrastructure vulnerability remediation on a predictable cycle with SLA reporting

Manage detection content as code, with reviewed and tested rules and documented runbooks 

- 
Have largely automated audit evidence on the infrastructure scope 

- 
Have eliminated long lived credentials on the critical paths, so engineering teams ship on secure defaults they did not have to think about

5+ years in infrastructure, cloud or platform engineering with a strong security focus, or in security engineering with hands on infrastructure practice 

- 
Production experience with Kubernetes: RBAC, network policies, admission controllers, secrets handling, workload identity, runtime security

Solid cloud experience, ideally Azure. Strong AWS or Google Cloud experience with a genuine interest in converting works too 

- 
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, GitOps workflows, CI/CD pipelines 

- 
Scripting and automation: Python or Go, plus shell. Comfortable reading and writing code, and opening pull requests on repositories owned by other teams

Log analysis and investigation: cloud audit logs, query languages, correlation across identity, network and application sources

Fluent English (US/UK) / B2 level or equivalent (FR).

title: Analytics Lead, Full Stack (Collections & Recoveries)
description:
Headquarters: Remote Canada

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

The Risk & Analytics team makes crucial decisions that direct Affirm’s business strategy. Our team designs and runs experiments to decide which product features to launch and which marketing campaigns to fund. We analyze performance not just to report on it, but to determine where to invest resources for maximum impact through building tools and analytical frameworks. We take ownership of the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision, ensuring Affirm grows efficiently and intelligently.

About the role 

The Collections & Recoveries Analyst will own and drive the collections and recoveries strategy for Affirm Canada, spanning the full post-delinquency lifecycle from early-stage digital and outbound collections through third-party recovery-agency placement and post-charge-off recoveries, partnering closely with Product and Compliance to ensure collections and recoveries practices meet Canadian federal and provincial consumer protection, collections, and privacy requirements. The analyst will be responsible for owning and driving the collections and recoveries roadmap for the market, quantifying the impact of new collections and recovery initiatives, and monitoring downstream performance.

The ideal candidate will have a combination of strong analytical expertise with a deep understanding of consumer credit and collections behaviour, and the ability to improve recovery outcomes through data-driven insights, vendor management, and cross-functional stakeholder management.

Come join us in our mission to change consumer finance through better data and technology, lower costs, and increased transparency while providing the best customer experience.

What you’ll do 

You will own the full Canadian post-delinquency lifecycle: digital and outbound collections, third-party agency placement, and post-charge-off recoveries.

- Collections channel strategy. Own the digital and calling collections mix: comms cadence and sequencing, day-of-week and channel optimisation, outbound calling strategy, and the experiments that prove what drives repayment.

- Recoveries Strategy. Own recoveries strategy and performance analytics: recovery rates, cost-to-collect, placement mix, liquidation curves, and vendor scorecards

- Strategy and roadmap ownership. Set and iterate the Canadian collections and recoveries strategy across delinquency, roll rates, agency performance, and charge-off / net-after-charge-off outcomes. You will identify, size and drive initiatives to improve collections and recoveries performance. 

- Initiative design and quantification. Take collections and recoveries initiatives from hypothesis to launch to measured impact: sizing the opportunity up front, developing A/B experiment frameworks, and proving the result afterwards.

- Regulatory partnership. Work with Product, Legal and Compliance so that every treatment you design holds up against Canada's distinctive regulatory landscape: province-by-province collection-agency and consumer protection legislation, Quebec's separate civil-law regime and consumer credit rules, and federal and provincial privacy laws.

- Cross-market leverage. Partner with collections and recoveries teams across other geographies, particularly the US, to drive cross-market leverage. 

What we look for 

- 5-7+ years in credit risk, collections, or recoveries strategy analytics in consumer lending.

- Experience designing or optimising collections and/or recoveries strategies leveraging data, analytics and insights. 

- Very strong analytical background with proficiency in SQL, Python, or other scripting languages.

- Demonstrated ability to interpret credit and collections performance data and translate it into action.

- Knowledge of collections, recoveries, and delinquency management practices. Familiarity with Canadian consumer protection, collections, and privacy regulations (e.g., provincial consumer protection / collection-agency legislation, PIPEDA) is a plus.

- Excellent cross-functional communication and stakeholder management with ability to communicate findings and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- A passion for finding insights in data and driving change based on those insights.

- Intelligence + Humility. Hubris is the fastest way to blow up a business!
