title: Senior Research Scientist - AI Safety Evaluations
description:
Why Faculty? 

We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here .

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the Team 

We are the central research and development team within Faculty's broader AI safety charter. Our group focuses on fundamental and applied technical AI safety research, producing rigorous scientific outputs - publications, tooling, technical reports & evaluations - that advance the theory, practice and understanding of AI risks, and directly inform the work of frontier AI labs, government agencies, and national security institutes.

Our research spans fundamental research using black-box and white-box approaches to understand and steer AI systems, to building and advancing safety evaluations which better understand and quantify risks in AI. We care deeply about mechanistic understanding and scientific rigour in measuring risks in AI systems. Current research threads include (but are not limited to) uncertainty calibration, goal drift, misinformation mitigation, steering vectors, robust safeguard measurement and the science of evaluations.

We collaborate closely with the Faculty's wider AI safety team, a group with a well-established track record in capability evaluations and red-teaming for misuse risk across CBRN, cybersecurity, societal and psychosocial harms. That work has been conducted for several leading frontier model developers and national safety institutes, and has been featured in model cards and safety reports from Anthropic, GDM, Meta & OpenAI.

About the role

As a Senior Research Scientist at Faculty, you will lead the development of cutting-edge safety evaluations to quantify AI risks in critical domains like CBRN and Cyber. Joining our high-impact R&D team, you will drive original research that advances safety methodology while collaborating with delivery teams building evaluations and red-teaming for frontier labs. This is a high-agency opportunity to conduct technical AI safety research that produces scientific outputs shaping the future of safe real-world AI deployment.

What you'll be doing

- Leading the development of novel safety evaluations in high-impact domains such as CBRN and Cyber to quantify emerging risks.

- Executing original technical research in AI safety evaluation methods, taking ideas from concept to publication.

- Shaping the R&D agenda by identifying strategic opportunities to advance safety evaluation methodology across Faculty and the broader ecosystem.

- Contributing thought leadership and deep technical expertise to client delivery projects, evaluation work, and red-teaming for frontier labs.

- Representing Faculty’s scientific leadership through active external engagement with the global research community, frontier labs, and government stakeholders.

Who we're looking for

- A track record of owning research end-to-end —from identifying novel problems to publication—driven by scientific curiosity and tenacity.

- Hands-on experience designing and building AI evaluations or benchmarks, alongside a strong ability to reason about construct validity and mitigate confounds.

- Expertise in red-teaming , adversarial testing, jailbreaking, indirect prompt injection, and assessing the robustness of model safeguards.

- Strong foundational skills in experimental design, statistical analysis, and uncertainty quantification, including Bayesian methods.

- Deep knowledge of language models, generative AI architectures, training methodologies, and safety mitigation techniques.

- Solid Python proficiency combined with the engineering discipline required to build robust, reproducible research.

Nice to haves

- Experience in threat and risk modelling.

- Background or knowledge in high-risk domains such as CBRN or Cybersecurity.

- A history of high-impact AI research, evidenced by top-tier publications or equivalent practical achievements.

Our Recruitment Ethos 

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. 

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: QA Engineer
description:
About Foundation Health 

Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy.

We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other.

The Role 

You'd be one of the first QA hires in the UK, working alongside our UK QA Lead to build how we do quality here: frameworks, standards and process, with no legacy test debt to dig out of. Everybody here is hands-on, and that's what this role is: in the detail, every day.

Before anything we build reaches a pharmacist's queue in the US, someone has to decide it's ready. That's you. If you take pride in what ships, and you'll say "this isn't ready" even when everyone wants it out the door, you'll fit right in.

We've built an AI operating system for pharmacies, tackling the operational infrastructure behind things like paperwork and care coordination. It's in production with enterprise health systems across the US, and we're working directly with one of the biggest names in pharmacy.

What you'll actually do 

- Help shape our UK QA practice with the QA Lead: frameworks, standards and how we work day to day

- Write automated tests in Playwright and test our APIs with Postman, across a serverless stack of Node.js, TypeScript, SvelteKit and GCP

- Test AI-powered features in production, including agentic workflows and LLM outputs, and help build the evals that tell us whether they're behaving

- Do proper manual testing, regression and UAT when a release needs it, and know when that beats automation

- Work closely with engineers to catch issues early, so moving fast never comes at the cost of the product

Who you are 

- You've got the experience . You have 3+ years in QA or software testing, with solid work on web apps and APIs.

- You're strong with Playwright . You also have a good instinct for when to automate and when to test by hand.

- You know what's at stake . You've worked on enterprise products, so you understand what happens when something breaks.

- You actually use AI . It's already part of how you work, or you've tested AI-powered products and know why it's a different problem.

- You care about the outcome . Quality matters to you as a result, not as a process to tick off.

The setup 

Hybrid, Manchester city centre, 1-2 days a week in the office. When you're working out what "correct" even means for an AI system, a whiteboard and the right three people in a room beat a Slack thread every time.

Not local? We offer relocation support for the right person.

We're Series A, there's early equity, and the work genuinely changes how people get their medication.

title: Software Engineer,  Financial Data & Payments
description:
Headquarters: Denver, CO - Hybrid; New York, NY - Hybrid; San Francisco, CA - Hybrid; Seattle, WA - Remote

About Gusto 

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role: 

We’re hiring seasoned engineers to join our teams that work on the financial backbone of Gusto's money movement — the ledger, reconciliation, and reporting systems that account for every dollar, and the payment profile that determines how employers fund payroll and how employees and contractors get paid. As a Gusto Software Engineer at this level, you’ll be guiding projects end-to-end by driving large technical architectural decisions (focusing on scale and modularity), understanding how to take existing systems closer to desired end states, executing on projects, and maintaining code that powers core experiences. If you’re interested in building elegant software with far-reaching effects in our modern economy, join us!

About the Team: 

Financial Data & Payment Profile (FDPP) sits inside Gusto's Payments organization, which moves money safely between partners, employers, employees, government authorities, and Gusto. FDPP owns the two things that every one of those movements depends on.

Financial Data is the system of record for the money itself: the ledger and subledger behind every payment, the reconciliation that proves our books agree with our banks and partners, the investigation of the variances that surface when they do not, and the financial reporting that Accounting, Finance, and Compliance depend on. When Gusto needs to answer where a dollar is — and prove it — the answer comes from systems this team builds.

Payment Profile is what makes a payment possible in the first place: the payment methods available to a customer, the bank accounts and connections behind them, the verification that makes those accounts trustworthy, and the profile state that decides whether a payment can happen at all. Hundreds of thousands of businesses depend on this being right the first time — and on it recovering gracefully when a bank account, a connection, or a preference changes.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: 

- Design, build, and test the financial data systems that record every dollar Gusto moves — the ledger and subledger that serve as the system of record, the transaction models underneath them, and the financial reporting that Accounting, Finance, Compliance, and our partners rely on to close the books

- Build reconciliation at Gusto's scale: prove that our internal records agree with bank, processor, and partner statements, and make the breaks that fall out of that comparison traceable rather than mysterious

- Lead variance investigation end-to-end — the tooling, instrumentation, and runbooks that turn "the numbers don't tie" into a specific root cause, and then into a fix that eliminates the whole class of break

- Own the payment profile: how employers are set up to fund payroll and how employees and contractors are set up to be paid — the payment methods available and the rules that govern which apply to whom, the bank accounts and connections behind them, and the verification state that determines whether money can move at all

- Make setup and verification something a small business can finish on its own — instant bank verification, graceful handling of broken or revoked connections, and a clear path back to a payable state when something changes

- Help scale one of the largest Ruby/Rails and TypeScript/React applications in the world

- Collaborate on complex and ambiguous problems with partnerships from Engineering, Product Management, Design, Data Science, Accounting, Finance, Compliance, Operations, and other cross-functional teams

- Mentor and grow fellow engineers working to create holistic and scalable solutions

Here’s what we're looking for: 

- Successful applicants have at least 10+ years of experience and the enthusiasm for a collaborative, test-driven environment

- Experience building fault-tolerant, mission-critical software as well as designing and developing robust, distributed systems using multiple general-purpose programming languages

- Experience influencing and guiding the work of multiple teams on scaling, refactoring, and optimizing legacy products 

- Experience architecting, building, and testing large-scale production level code that is maintainable, structured, and well-documented

- An aptitude and interest in bringing clarity and simplicity to complex and ambiguous problems

- Ability to communicate technical complexity and help facilitate informed tradeoffs

- Experience in one or more of these domains is strongly preferred: ledger or subledger design, financial reconciliation, accounting systems, or payments infrastructure

- Comfort with double-entry accounting concepts — journal entries, chart of accounts, debits and credits, and tying a subledger out to the general ledger — and the ability to work with accountants and controllers in their own vocabulary

- Experience building systems where correctness, auditability, and immutability matter more than raw throughput, and where a silent data error is worse than an outage

- Bonus: Experience with bank account verification, payment rails (ACH, wire, RTP), or third-party banking data and verification providers

- Bonus: Experience with Ruby on Rails, Typescript, and React

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $183,000-$200,000 /yr in Denver & most remote locations, and $222,000-$245,000 /yr for San Francisco, Seattle & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. 

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

title: Staff Product Engineer ( SaaS / Remote )
description:
Ready to own it, build it, and grow it? 

The Mission: 

Publitas lets people, and increasingly agents, create, host and distribute digital flyers and catalogues for retail brands. Our customers include ALDI, IKEA, Carrefour, Metro and Decathlon. Right now we’re building a fully automatic, agentic workflow that generates a whole catalogue from a brand guide and a list of products. 

As a Staff Product Engineer, you’ll build this product hands-on, taking open-ended problems to working software in whatever part of the stack the problem needs. You’ll join a team of senior engineers who are put on our hardest problems, some of which cut across teams. Our customer base is large (not Google scale, but big), so what you ship gets used, and it comes with real technical challenges. Our core stack is Ruby on Rails on the backend and JavaScript with React on the frontend, with services around it in JavaScript, TypeScript and Python. This is a staff-level role, and you’ll have a lot of influence in a mid-sized company with very little red tape. 

This role is for you if 

- You've built several complete products and you'd enjoy showing them to us. 

- You like open-ended problems, and you'd rather work out what to build than be handed a spec. 

- You enjoy problems that are hard to think through, and you can point to one you cracked. 

- You get excited about the end result, not just the code. 

- AI has changed what you dare to build: you ship faster, and you take on projects you’d never have started alone. 

- You want real influence in a mid-sized company with a large customer base and very little red tape. 

It's probably not for you if 

- You prefer to stay in one layer of the stack. 

- You want a detailed spec or a clear list of tasks before you start. 

- You're still trying AI out rather than building with it every day. 

Where and when you work 

The role is fully remote, and most of the stakeholders and peers work Central European hours. Nobody sets your schedule, but we'd like around six hours of overlap with the team on a normal day. In practice that works best if you live within about two hours of CET. 

Show us what you've built 

When you apply, point us to things you've made. Complete, working applications say the most, but libraries and tools are welcome too. We'd love to hear how you built them. 

What We Offer You to Win 

- Transparent Compensation : A competitive salary (geo-bracketed to your location in the EU) with a clear, performance-based path for career progression. 

- True Remote Autonomy : No clock-watching or useless alignment meetings. You manage your territory as if it were your own business. 

- Global Team Retreats : Working remotely shouldn't mean working isolated. We gather the entire company in inspiring cities across the globe once a year to connect, strategize, and celebrate in person. 

- Modern Sales Stack & Gear : A premium MacBook, remote work accessories, and a co-working budget if you want to work outside your home. 

- Personal Growth Budget : A monthly wellness allowance, an education/course budget to sharpen your skills, and free access to Kindle and Audible books. 

- Time Off : 25 days of paid vacation plus your local national holidays. 

At Publitas, we see AI as a core lever for performance, efficiency, and innovation. We expect all team members to actively use AI in their daily work to improve quality, speed, and output. 

Depending on the role, this ranges from effectively using AI tools in day-to-day workflows to designing and scaling AI-driven systems. We are not looking for candidates who are “AI-curious”; we look for people who already use AI to do better work and can demonstrate tangible impact.

title: Senior Growth Marketer, Web & Experimentation
description:
Our Growth Marketers bring buyers to datasnipper.com through integrated campaigns. You'll turn that traffic into demo requests and pipeline. You'll run A/B tests, personalize the site, work on conversion rate optimization (CRO), and manage the projects that add new functionality to our websites. You'll also bring AI into the website program, building on the AI that already runs our go-to-market.

You'll work from one ranked backlog and report each week on what moved conversion. You'll form hypotheses from data, get them built with our designer and developer, and roll out the winners.

Your closest partners are the Growth Marketers, our Senior Web Experience Designer and Senior Web Developer, and GTM Engineering, which collects intent data from our website.

About DataSnipper 

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals to make those judgements. With Alwin by DataSnipper, our new agentic platform, AI agents now take on end-to-end audit and finance procedures, while every conclusion stays traceable to its source. That frees professionals to focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

We're trusted by Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. Today, more than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on our platform, and in 2025 alone DataSnipper delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to its customers.

Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, we've built a strong foundation for what's next. And as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

Alwin has just launched, demand is growing, and we're expanding into new markets and segments. With a product customers already rely on, there's a huge opportunity to make your mark.

Where the website stands today

Most of our inbound pipeline starts on datasnipper.com . Until now, our Senior Growth Marketer handled CRO on the side, and many people on the Marketing team publish pages, update content individually. In short, very fragmented collaboration.

In an AI-dense market, that work counts for more. Anyone can generate volume now. What's hard, and what earns attention, is staying close to what our customers care about and bringing campaign ideas sharp enough to cut through. That's the work that sets this team apart, and what you'll be part of.

Our tracking needs a cleanup before we can trust test results. Localized landing pages come next: Japan, DACH and France need web experiences in their own language. GTM Engineering already scores visitor intent by page, and we barely use that data on the site. Personalization by segment and market has barely started.

AI already runs parts of our go-to-market. Agents nurture leads, a classifier scores the intent behind every web visit, and we enrich accounts automatically. The website hasn't caught up.

Buyers also find us in new ways. More of them research software through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews before they ever reach our site.

The web team has a dedicated designer and developer. This role decides what we test next and reports what worked.

What you'll be doing

Run the experimentation program

- Build the testing roadmap for datasnipper.com and the localized sites, from hypothesis to rollout.

- Set the website's testing rules: minimum sample size, test duration, and when to call or stop a test.

- Keep a learning log that Growth, Sales and Product Marketing check before they propose a test.

- Report results in pipeline terms: demo requests, demo-to-SQL rate and pipeline per session.

Improve conversion where buyers decide

- Optimize the demo request flow and the pricing, product and campaign pages.

- Map the funnel from first visit to SQL in GA4 and HubSpot, find where buyers drop off, and fix it.

- Work with the Growth Marketers to match each campaign landing page to its ad, audience and market.

Personalize the site

- Tailor content, proof points and CTAs by vertical, market and buying stage.

- Use intent and enrichment data from GTM Engineering to decide who sees what.

- Test each localized site as it launches, to the same standard as the English site.

Build AI into the web program

- Use the intent and enrichment data we already collect to build pages that adapt to each visitor.

- Use AI to generate and localize test variants, so we test more ideas each month.

- Automate test QA, result analysis and weekly reporting, with a person signing off on the results.

- Prototype new AI experiences for buyers, such as an assistant that answers product and pricing questions.

Manage web projects

- Scope new website functionality, write the brief, and run delivery with our designer and developer.

- Turn requests from Product Marketing, Sales, Partnerships and Growth into a ranked backlog, and use data to decide what waits.

- Run QA and launch, then measure each project's result.

Keep the site findable and measurable

- Protect organic search and AI visibility in every test and launch: canonicals, page speed, schema markup and crawl access.

- Track traffic and demo requests referred by AI assistants, and test pages for buyers who arrive that way.

- Maintain website tracking with Marketing Operations in Google Tag Manager, GA4 and HubSpot.

- Build the weekly web performance view the team works from.

What we’re looking for

- 5+ years in CRO, web optimization or growth marketing, ideally in B2B SaaS. You've run an A/B testing program and can walk us through tests that won and tests that lost.

- Data fluency. You know when to trust a test result, and when sample size, novelty or segment noise undermine it. You pull your own numbers from GA4 and HubSpot.

- Structure. You run a backlog, write briefs a developer can build from, and keep several projects moving. You tell stakeholders each week what ships.

- Collaboration. You get work done through a designer, a developer and stakeholders who all want space on the website. You involve them before you set a hypothesis, and use data to settle priority disputes.

- AI builder. You’ve shipped something with AI that changed how a team works: an agent, an automated workflow, or a tool other people use. Bring the example and what broke first.

- Commercial focus. You judge tests on the pipeline they create.

Tools you'll work with (willingness to ramp & learn matters more than a complete checklist):

- Creative: Figma, Canva

- Website: Framer, Contentstack

- Analytics: HubSpot, Looker Studio, Supermetrics, Fibbler, Snowflake

- CRM and marketing automation: HubSpot

- Experimentation and personalization: Optimizely

- Behavior analytics: heatmaps and session recordings

- Project management and handoff: Linear, Figma

- AI: Claude Enterprise (Projects, Skills and MCP integrations), ChatGPT, and build tools such as Lovable or n8n

Bonus: hands-on technical SEO and a view on how AI search changes the way buyers find B2B software. SQL, or enough HTML, CSS and JavaScript to set up a test yourself.

Recruitment Process 

- Recruiter Screen (30 minutes, online)

- Hiring Manager Interview (30 minutes, online)

- Assessment Interview (1 hour, on-site)

- Final Interview (30 minutes, online)

We welcome applicants regardless of age, race, ethnicity, nationality, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or any other characteristic that makes you, you. 

What matters to us is what you can bring to the role, the team, and DataSnipper. 🚀

title: Software Engineer
description:
THE POSITION 

Our roster has an opening with your name on it

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our CPE Platform vertical, working within Core Products and Experiences. In this role, you’ll contribute to a multidisciplinary team building reliable, engaging products for millions of players. You’ll bring some hands-on engineering experience, a practical approach to solving problems, and a willingness to learn from and support others. You’ll help deliver well-structured software, take part in technical discussions, and contribute to documentation, collaboration, and continuous improvement across the team.

We are a growth company so there are plenty of opportunities for you to learn and grow with us, plus we have remote-first working and a generous paid leave policy to enjoy your downtime. We’re committed to making sure everyone who works here can maintain a healthy work/life balance.

THE GAME PLAN 

Everyone on our team has a part to play

- You’ll work as part of our Session Management team, helping build and improve backend services that support reliable, scalable customer sessions

- You’ll learn how our systems work and contribute to well-scoped features, fixes and improvements with support from more experienced engineers

- You’ll write clear, maintainable backend code using Java or similar languages, following team standards and best practices

- You’ll help build and improve APIs, services and database-backed functionality that can handle high volumes of traffic

- You’ll test your changes carefully and look for simple ways to make our services more reliable, observable and easier to support

- You’ll take part in code reviews, design discussions, planning sessions and team ceremonies, asking questions and sharing ideas

- You’ll investigate bugs and support issues, working with the team to understand root causes and make practical improvements

- You’ll learn about scaling systems, databases, caching and cloud infrastructure through hands-on work with the team

- You’ll keep documentation up to date so others can understand how our services work and how to support them

- You’ll collaborate closely with engineers, product partners and stakeholders to deliver changes that improve the reliability and performance of session management

- You’ll bring curiosity, humility and a willingness to learn, while growing your engineering judgement and technical confidence over time

What We’re Looking For 

THE STATS 

What we’re looking for in our next teammate

- Some experience building backend software through work, internships, placements, bootcamps, university projects or personal projects

- An understanding of Java or a similar object-oriented programming language, and an interest in developing backend services and APIs

- Familiarity with databases and SQL, with an interest in learning more about data modelling, performance and scaling

- Awareness of common data structures, algorithms and software design principles

- An interest in distributed systems, reliability, monitoring and how high-traffic backend systems operate in production

- Familiarity with cloud technologies, containers or CI/CD is helpful, but not required

- An understanding of testing basics and a willingness to write tests as part of everyday development

- Comfortable working in a team environment, asking questions, receiving feedback and learning from others

- A practical approach to problem solving and a desire to leave code and documentation clearer than you found it

- Enthusiasm for working on backend systems that support customer-facing products at scale

What You Can Expect 

- Interesting work - working in a fast-paced and ever-changing industry, new problems and exciting solutions are never too far away. There are always opportunities to learn new skills and broaden your horizons

- A sense of achievement - Our teams own their own software and when that awesome new feature ships to users and the positive feedback starts rolling in, you can feel really proud of what you and your team created

- Personal development - clear and defined career pathways for every role at every level, a supportive manager, loads of learning opportunities and even 10% of your time to dedicate to your learning.

- Belonging - everyone at FanDuel works for each other, we win together, make mistakes together and have lots of fun doing it.

- Trust - A trusting work environment where productivity is valued above all else, giving you autonomy and ownership of your time and work

- Great financial package - Including salary, bonus, pension, private healthcare, share save scheme, flexible working & holiday policy along with a number of other benefits.

ABOUT FANDUEL 

FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product. 

In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.

The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.

FanDuel Group is a subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, the world's largest sports betting and gaming operator with a portfolio of globally recognized brands and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FLUT).

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 

FanDuel is an equal opportunities employer. Diversity and inclusion in FanDuel means that we respect and value everyone as individuals. We don't tolerate bias, judgement or harassment. Our focus is on developing employees so that they reach their full potential. 

FanDuel is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please email Benefits@fanduel.com .

title: Software Engineer II: Autonomous Supply Chains
description:
About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains

About Flexport

Look around you. Almost everything in the room crossed an ocean to get there. Moving one container from a factory to a warehouse takes 10 to 15 companies: truckers, customs brokers, port terminals, ocean carriers, insurers, lenders and warehouses, each with its own systems, paperwork and rules. A freight forwarder runs that whole journey, so the brand that makes the goods doesn't have to.

Most forwarders still run it on email, spreadsheets and phone calls. We call it email freight forwarding. Flexport runs it on one platform, where AI agents do the routine work and experts step in where judgment matters. We've moved $175B of goods for more than 13,000 brands across 135 countries. Our agents handle 21 million tasks a year, and up to 80% of customs work is automated.

Global logistics is a $13 trillion industry, and even the largest forwarder earns less than 3% of global logistics outsourcing revenue. People-powered operations don't scale: to grow, you hire. Software broke that ceiling for taxis with Uber, and for payments with Adyen and Stripe. Freight is next.

Amsterdam is one of Flexport's six engineering hubs, alongside San Francisco, Seattle, Chicago, Shanghai and Shenzhen. We own four domains end to end: Customs Technology, Autonomous Supply Chains (Applied AI), Platform and Security. See what we build at amsterdam-engineering.flexport.com .

The team: Autonomous Supply Chains

Logistics is famously hard to automate, because the happy path rarely happens. One customer won't take deliveries on a Tuesday. Another wants invoices only on Fridays, with some lines merged and others renamed. Until recently, people handled all of that by hand. Now operators use Forge, the agentic platform we build, to automate their own work: catching anomalies, routing exceptions, escalating stuck containers and adjusting invoices to each customer. Forge remembers every customer's rules and learns from every workflow run, so it gets smarter every day.

Autonomous Supply Chains is our Applied AI team: small, senior and reporting to the VP of Engineering. Self-driving cars are rated from level 0 to level 5. Most of the freight industry still runs at level 0: people emailing spreadsheets. Our goal is level 5 for freight, with Forge as the best agentic platform there is, handling every complexity, every calamity and every odd preference without skipping a beat.

Stack: TypeScript, Rust, Next.js, Temporal, Postgres and Snowflake, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

The role

As an Applied AI Engineer II on Autonomous Supply Chains, you'll build the agents and AI-powered applications that make Flexport's operations faster and increasingly autonomous. You'll find the most painful problems in our operations, design the solution and ship it to operators moving freight across 135 countries. This isn't a role where you join a team and pick up tickets.

What you'll do

- Design and ship end-to-end AI agents that handle real logistics work, such as customs compliance, document processing, invoice validation and exception management.

- Build the evaluation, guardrails and human-in-the-loop flows that make an agent trustworthy enough to run 24/7.

- Stay on top of what's happening in the world of AI, and channel those innovations straight into the product. When Jev came out this fall, we had three use cases live within two weeks.

- Work directly with operators, domain experts and leadership to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products, and measure whether they worked.

- Move fast from idea to production, and treat every deployment as a chance to learn.

- Cross organizational boundaries to understand problems deeply and get things done without waiting for permission.

You should have

- 3+ years of software engineering experience, and you've built seriously with LLMs, whether in production, in side projects or just because you couldn't stop yourself.

- LLM fluency: agent patterns, tool use, RAG, prompt design and evaluation. You know the difference between what works in production and what looks good in a demo.

- Full-stack capability in TypeScript and Next.js. You can own a feature end to end.

- Product instinct: you can tell what's worth building, not just how to build it.

- Clear written and spoken communication in English, including design docs that people actually read.

Nice to have

- Experience with workflow orchestration, such as Temporal.

- Experience building internal tools or operator-facing applications.

How we work

- We value builders. People who think end to end, do their own discovery and ship independently. Nobody hands you a spec.

- Your users sit next to you. Operators, customs experts and account teams work in the same office. Watch them use your tool, and fix it before dessert.

- Any model, any harness. Use any frontier model from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, in all the popular coding harnesses. Our engineers manage swarms of coding agents from their first week.

- We ship dozens of times a day, with continuous deployment and a platform team obsessed with making it safe and fast.

- Hybrid, in English. We're together in our office on Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, a few minutes from Dam Square, three days a week*. The other days are flexible. English is our working language, and we work daily with colleagues in the US and China.

- No logistics background needed. Almost nobody joins knowing what an HTS code or a bill of lading is. The experts sit a few desks away.

- Agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why this role is special

- Your work is visible: a small, senior team that reports to the VP of Engineering. What you build gets noticed, and your ideas shape the direction.

- Real stakes: your agents act on real shipments for 13,000+ brands in 135 countries, so the impact is immediate and measurable.

- You're early: the playbook for applied AI in logistics hasn't been written yet. You'll help write it.

What's in it for you

- Equity for everyone: every team member becomes a shareholder in a pre-IPO company in a multi-trillion dollar industry.

- 25 vacation days, based on full-time employment, plus Dutch public holidays.

- Health insurance, fully paid: a collective plan with basic and additional packages. Flexport pays the monthly premium.

- Pension: a defined contribution scheme.

- Breakfast and lunch: daily catered lunch with vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and drinks in the office.

- Commute covered: Flexport covers home-to-office commuting costs if you live outside Amsterdam.

- Parental leave: time off for both parents to bond with a new child.

- Wellbeing support: an Employee Assistance Program through Aetna for you and your household, at no cost.

- Visa sponsorship: we sponsor visas for the right candidates and help you move to Amsterdam. Eligible international hires may also benefit from the Dutch expat tax ruling.

Our hiring process

- Application review: our team reviews your application.

- Recruiter screen: talk about your experience, the role and your questions about Flexport.

- Remote coding: your first coding interview takes place over video.

- Onsite coding and system design: a second coding interview and system design in our office.

- Project deep dive: discuss a project from your experience with the hiring manager.

- Team debrief: the interview team reviews feedback together. You don't attend this step.

- Offer: if there's a match, your recruiter walks you through the offer.

An additional remote coding round may be needed if the earlier coding interviews leave questions to resolve. Your recruiter will confirm the plan before interviews begin. We only contact candidates from ----- addresses, and we will never ask you for money or banking details.

Commitment to equal opportunity

At Flexport, our ability to fulfill our mission of making global commerce easy and accessible relies on having a diverse, dedicated and engaged workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, health status, marital and family status, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Money
description:
Headquarters: New York, New York; Miami, Florida; Remote (USA)

About the Company 

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Money 

The Money Team owns the financial infrastructure that underpins every dollar and crypto asset that moves through Gemini. We build and operate the ledger platform — the system of record for all crypto and fiat balances, settlements, fees, rewards, and administrative adjustments — as well as the payments services and reconciliation pipelines that connect Gemini to banks, payment rails, and external partners.

Our systems are relied upon by finance, compliance, treasury, and regulatory reporting. Correctness is non-negotiable. If something is ambiguous, we clarify it. If something is manual, we automate it. If something is unsafe, we fix it.

The Role: Senior Software Engineer 

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join a team of ledger and financial infrastructure engineers designing, building, and operating core money-movement systems at scale. You'll work on services that must handle high transaction volumes, evolve safely as new products and partners are introduced, and remain easy to operate and audit.

Responsibilities: 

- Design, develop, deploy, and support ledger and payments services that accurately record all crypto and fiat money movement across the platform. 

- Build and evolve bank settlement and reconciliation pipelines that connect Gemini to external payment rails and banking partners. 

- Apply sound engineering principles to identify correctness, consistency, and operational risks — and implement safeguards in software before they become incidents.

- Partner with finance, reconciliation, and treasury teams to understand real-world workflows and translate them into robust, auditable system behavior. 

- Design scalable APIs and data models that support new transaction types, products, and regulatory requirements without increasing operational burden. 

- Write well-tested, production-grade code that other critical systems depend on.

- Monitor and communicate the health of ledger and payment systems, proactively identify issues, and participate in incident response and remediation.

- Mentor teammates to ensure new functionality is correct, auditable, and production-ready.

- Participate in on-call rotations as needed.

Minimum Qualifications: 

- 5+ years of experience building backend systems in a production environment.

- Strong experience designing and operating distributed, stateful systems where data integrity is critical. 

- Proficiency in at least one backend language — we primarily use Scala and Go, but are open to candidates willing to learn. 

- Experience with unit testing, integration testing, and CI/CD pipelines.

- Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

- Ability to reason about and debug complex system behavior across services and data stores.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with cross-functional partners.

Preferred Qualifications: 

- Experience working on ledger systems, accounting platforms, payments infrastructure, or financial transaction processing. 

- Familiarity with double-entry bookkeeping, reconciliation processes, audit requirements, or regulatory reporting. 

- Experience integrating with external payment rails or banking partners (ACH, wire, card networks). 

- Familiarity with workflow orchestration systems (e.g. Temporal, Cadence) for durable, retryable financial processes. 

- Background in fintech or financial services.

It Pays to Work Here 

The compensation & benefits package for this role includes:

- Competitive starting pay

- A discretionary annual bonus

- Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant

- Comprehensive health plans

- 401K with company matching

- Paid Parental Leave

- Flexible time off

Salary Range : The base salary range for this role is between $140,000 - $200,000 in the State of New York. This range is not inclusive of our discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Expectations may vary by location and role, so candidates are encouraged to connect with their recruiter to learn more about the specific policy for the role. Employees who do not live near one of our hubs are part of our remote workforce. All employees, however, are required to onboard in-person at one of our office locations. 

At Gemini, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our products, and we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. title: Power Platform Technical Architect
description:
Ludia Consulting is one of the fastest growing and innovative consulting firms in Microsoft Dynamics Finance & Supply Chain, Customer Engagement and Power Platform. We are looking for a team member that is committed to helping others and their communities while also growing professionally as part of our Ludia family.

We are not just a traditional organization; we are driven to help our partners and clients while delivering value every day. Our team members are also encouraged to grow by sharing their knowledge and experience through a multitude of community-driven channels, including local non-profit organizations.

The Role

As a Power Platform Technical Architect, you will be a key aspect of our mission to translate business and functional requirements into scalable, secure technical architectures using modern design principles and best practices in software development for our customers and internal initiatives. You will own the technical and integration architecture for client engagements, set technical direction and standards for delivery teams, and communicate architectural decisions, effort estimates, and risks to solution architects, management, and clientele.

This position combines deep hands-on technical expertise with an equally important emphasis on architectural judgment and technical leadership. To achieve success, our architects demonstrate the ability to learn quickly, communicate ideas effectively, define and lead team efforts and utilize flexibility and creativity to present a variety of solutions. You must have excellent communication, analytical, architecture, and technical leadership skills to excel in this role.

Essential Functions

- Own the end-to-end technical architecture for Power Platform and Dynamics 365 engagements, leading technical discovery, requirements analysis, evaluation of solution options, and design decisions with client and project stakeholders.
- Architect Dataverse solutions and guide their configuration and development using model-driven apps, Power Automate cloud flows, business rules, Power Fx, and other platform capabilities, remaining hands-on for complex or high-risk components.
- Determine when and how to extend the platform using C#, .NET, plug-ins, custom APIs, JavaScript, Dataverse Web API, REST APIs, and custom connectors, and establish coding standards and reusable patterns for those extensions.
- Define the integration architecture and patterns for secure inbound and outbound integrations using Dataverse and relevant Azure services, including authentication, error handling, retry behavior, performance, and operational support.
- Define logical data models, data mappings, migration and synchronization approaches, alternate keys, and data-quality controls.
- Define non-functional requirements and design for security, scalability, performance, service protection limits, licensing, and cost.
- Establish Dataverse security models and platform governance, including environment strategy, Managed Environments, and DLP policies.
- Author and govern architecture artifacts, including technical designs, architecture decision records, integration diagrams, process flows, estimates, assumptions, risks, deployment plans, runbooks, and support documentation.
- Define and govern the application lifecycle management strategy using solutions, dependency and layer management, environment variables, connection references, source control, Power Platform Pipelines, and CI/CD automation.
- Establish quality standards and lead code and design reviews, test strategy, solution validation, performance and capacity planning, and release readiness.
- Serve as the technical escalation point for complex production issues, lead root-cause analysis, and define monitoring and supportability standards for managed services.
- Lead technical walkthroughs, communicate progress and risks, mentor and develop consultants and developers, and collaborate effectively across disciplines and time zones.
- Support pre-sales and scoping by shaping technical approaches, validating estimates, and identifying delivery risks for proposals and statements of work.
- Maintain current knowledge of the platform roadmap and shape internal practices, reference architectures, reusable assets, and knowledge sharing.
Skills & Competencies

- At least eight years of hands-on consulting or development experience with Microsoft Power Platform and Dynamics 365, including at least two years in a technical architect or technical lead role.
- Experience delivering multiple end-to-end enterprise Power Platform or Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement implementations as the lead technical architect or technical lead.
- Advanced hands-on experience with Dataverse, model-driven apps, Power Automate cloud flows, data modeling, and platform configuration.
- Practical development experience with C#, .NET, JavaScript, REST APIs, and Dataverse extension patterns.
- Deep expertise in synchronous and asynchronous integration patterns, authentication, error handling, performance, and supportability, including Azure integration services such as Azure Functions, Logic Apps, Service Bus, Event Grid, API Management, and Key Vault.
- Experience with solution-based application lifecycle management, source control, automated deployments, and tools such as Power Platform CLI, Azure DevOps, or GitHub.
- Experience designing Dataverse security and troubleshooting application, automation, integration, and deployment issues.
- Ability to create clear technical documentation, develop reliable estimates, identify risks and assumptions, and explain and defend architectural decisions and trade-offs to technical, business, and executive audiences.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, organization, prioritization, and collaboration skills, including experience working independently within distributed teams.
- Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor technical teams, set design and coding standards, and review the work of developers and consultants.
Desirable Experience

title: Product Engineer (TypeScript)
description:
Our team shared’s mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect 

We believe healthcare shouldn’t be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better.

Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care.

Already trusted by 15 000+ providers, we’re transforming the patient–provider relationship, one call at a time.

Want to shape the future of healthcare?

Join us ! 

- Discover our company culture and values 

- Here is a product teaser 

- Eliott's interview for Welcome to the jungle 

- Eliott's quick interview for Speedinvest 

- Articles on our A round ( techfundingnews , Maddyness , les echos , our blog )

Vocca in a few words 

Vocca is an AI voice agent that answers 100% of the calls of medical centres. The patient calls, the AI books the appointment or answers the question, and the medical secretaries keep their time for the cases where a human is really needed.

- $20M raised, with the founders of Alan and Datadog as investors

- Close to 1 million calls a month going through the platform

- More than 1,000 medical staff use our product all day

The problem 

Every medical centre has its own rules. Who can book what, with which practitioner, at what time, what to do with an urgent case at 6 pm. Today these rules live in prompts and in the heads of our ops team. Each new clinic takes hours of manual work, and the ops team is the bottleneck of our growth.

We are building the platform that removes that bottleneck. A scenario engine where the behaviour of the agent is structured configuration, not free text. A self-serve onboarding where a clinic connects its software and sets itself up. A dashboard where the medical staff stop executing and start supervising: the agent handles the volume, humans check what matters.

This is the difference between selling a service and selling a product. The long term vision is simple: a clinic signs, connects its software and is live within days, without a single developer involved. You would be building that.

What you will own 

- The scenario engine and its configuration model. One product that handles the rules of thousands of medical centres without becoming a swamp.

- The self-serve onboarding, from the backend to the dashboard. Internal tooling already took a clinic deployment from days to under an hour. The next step is zero developer ticket on a standard onboarding.

- The dashboard our clinics use all day. Fast, reliable and clean enough that a medical secretary prefers it to the phone. We take frontend quality seriously and follow a design system written in code.

- Your features, end to end. From the spec with the ops team to production, and the fix when something breaks, with the reason it does not happen again.

How we build 

- Experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a result, not a debate.

- Ship, then fix the last 1%. We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. The judgment about what not to touch is yours.

- AI, seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks.

- Close to the field. Every change lands in front of more than 1,000 medical staff. You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics and the sales team that sells the product.

Stack 

TypeScript everywhere, backend and frontend (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, a design system written in code. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.

Who does well here 

- 3 to 8 years building full-stack products in production, in startups that were growing fast.

- You stayed long enough somewhere to see a system live, break and get better, and you learned from it.

- TypeScript is your main language, backend and frontend, not a line on your CV. You have a real eye for interface quality and the discipline to follow a design system.

- You think about the product and the business as much as the code, and you know how to build systems that hold when the volume explodes.

- You move without waiting for a perfect frame: you try, you propose, you ship. You ask for help when you are stuck.

- You had good practices before AI: solid system design, clean refactoring and a good nose for the risks of generated code that nobody tested.

Probably not for you if you need every feature fully specified before you start

What we expect from you 

- First week. Onboarded on the stack, your first improvement on the dashboard is in production.

- First month. You own one feature end to end, from the spec with the ops team to production, without mockups or hand-holding.

- First 3 months. The first version of the scenario engine is in production. A standard clinic can be onboarded without a developer ticket.

- 6 to 12 months. Most new clinics are live within 7 days. Clinics configure their own rules in the dashboard.

Process: 4 steps, fast 

- 45 min with Nans (Talent).

- 45 min with Pierrick, Head of Engineering.

- 1h30 in our office with the engineering team: coding without AI and a real conversation about product architecture.

- 30 min with Hugo, CTO.

Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.

Practical 

- Paris, rue d'Alexandrie (Sentier), new offices.

- Hybrid, 3 days at the office.

- BSPCE.

- Claude Max provided.

We aim to keep the process within 30 days . You’ll receive continuous feedback throughout.

Why should you join Vocca? 

- An entrepreneurial adventure , with a supportive, high-energy, execution-focused team

- A product already live , with delighted customers in a fast-growing market (healthcare automation, voice AI)

- A true scaling phase , with everything still to build

- Real responsibilities from day one

We hire people, not roles. 

If you're excited about our opportunities but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success. If you identify yourself as a woman : Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

title: Software Engineer - Global Memberships Platform
description:
Our Global Structure 

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Software Engineer - Global Memberships Platform 

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day.

From real-time logistics to resilient infrastructure and marketplace optimisation, we design, build and operate technology that powers growth at a global scale for all three of our brands: Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt.

Our team, Global Membership Platform, owns the core platform capabilities that drive the subscription model, which is key to our business. We build and run the shared services behind how customers join, manage and benefit from our membership offerings, giving every brand a single, reliable and scalable foundation to launch and evolve its membership proposition. Because membership is a paid product, we work closely with the Money team on payments, from how members are charged and billed to how payment outcomes feed back into their membership, so correctness and reliability are central to what we build. As a new team, we have a clear mandate and plenty of room to shape it: designing platform services that work across brands and regions, keeping a business-critical, always-on system dependable, and partnering with engineers, product and design teams across Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt to bring membership together as one global platform.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our London team. In this role, you’ll help us build and maintain high-performance systems that power our global marketplace, ensuring a seamless experience for millions of users. This role is based in our London office with a hybrid setup, typically 3 days in the office.

Get to know our Engineering team — what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

What You’ll Be Doing 

You’ll be joining a multi-disciplinary engineering team focused on technical execution and collaboration. As a Software Engineer at Deliveroo, your individual work contributes to achieving goals across your team, simplifying the maintenance of production systems while ensuring operational readiness and health.

Here’s what your day-to-day might look like:

- Drive Technical Excellence: Improve code structure and architecture across your team’s remit, developing, releasing and running large-scale web applications whilst transitioning our monolithic codebase to a microservice-based architecture

- Lead Project Planning: Foresee dependencies and risks, partnering closely with Product and Design to ensure smooth delivery of complex features, whilst defining the backend architecture and tech stack for a product area

- Optimise Operations: Improve performance, reliability, scalability and security for our backend systems

- Collaborate & Influence: Build relationships across global engineering teams to identify collaboration opportunities and influence the wider technical roadmap.

- Mentor & Hire: Support the personal growth of your colleagues through technical guidance and take an active role in conducting engineering interviews to scale our team.

What You’ll Need to Thrive 

Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

- Proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software 

- Strong Engineering Principles: Deep pride in writing readable, well-designed, and well-tested software.

- Backend Expertise: Significant experience building web-based applications (we use Go, Ruby/Rails, Python, Scala, and Rust).

- Data Proficiency: Practical experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL) and "NoSQL" backends like Redis, DynamoDB, or ElasticSearch.

- Systems at Scale: Proven ability to manage web architecture at scale (handling 20krpm and above).

- Technical Leadership: Experience breaking down large pieces of work and guiding implementation choices for a team of engineers.

Why Join Us? 

At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving. We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.

🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog .

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role 

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, based in Poland, you'll build backend systems that help GitLab engineers trust the software they create with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but passing tests don't always mean the software works as intended. You'll contribute to validation approaches and feedback mechanisms that help agents catch that gap and self-correct while they work.

This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We’re looking for someone who has built with agents, run into the gap between passing tests and working software, and wants to help close it.

What you’ll do 

- Own backend features from design through production rollout, making the design calls within the architecture the team agrees on.

- Build agentic code-review and validation workflows that check whether generated code does what was intended, not just whether its tests pass.

- Prototype focused validation and feedback mechanisms with your teammates, and use what you learn to improve the platform.

- Develop language-aware validation approaches, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, adapting techniques to each language while applying a shared definition of trusted software to assess whether agent-generated code delivers the intended behavior.

- Implement feedback that helps agents identify problems and self-correct during development.

- Collaborate with engineering teams to test these approaches in real workflows, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those measurements to evaluate improvements.

- Participate in code and design reviews, explain implementation trade-offs, and seek feedback on your work.

- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring 

- Hands-on experience building software with artificial intelligence agents and understanding why their output can pass tests yet fail to behave as intended, from encountering that gap yourself or building something to prevent it.

- Backend development experience in at least one of Rust, Ruby, Go, or Python, with openness to working across languages.

- Experience taking backend features from design into production, discussing implementation trade-offs, and knowing when to ask for guidance.

- Comfort working inside a large existing codebase, not only on greenfield projects.

- A practical approach to prototyping, learning from results, and turning useful ideas into working software.

- Clear written communication and the ability to collaborate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.

- The ability to share decisions transparently and improve your work through iteration and feedback.

- Familiarity with containerized services; Kubernetes experience is a plus.

About the team 

The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.
